subject: Discovery recap: Observability & evals — ZenHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@zenhealth.com>, Priya Rao <priya@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-25T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: Observability & evals — ZenHealth

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Below is a concise recap of the pain, success criteria, current stack, and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive. Please flag anything I missed.

Pain points / business impact
- Regression risk after model changes: several recent updates caused a 6–8% drop in accuracy on critical patient triage prompts (manual rollback required).
- Lack of per-prompt observability: hard to surface prompt families causing regressions, and no easy way to trace from a UI incident to the exact prompt/token sequence.
- Cost & latency visibility gaps: token-level cost and tail-latency per route are opaque; teams want to correlate cost vs. quality.

Current stack (from our discussion)
- Models: hybrid — internal models hosted on AWS SageMaker endpoints + some third-party API calls for non-sensitive routes.
- Logging/monitoring: Datadog for infra-level metrics; ad-hoc dashboards for API-level success rates.
- Evals: ad-hoc CSV-based golden prompt sets and manual spot checks currently run by QA.

Success criteria for a pilot with Redwood
- Detect regressions against golden prompt sets automatically (alerting + daily regression report).
- Per-route dashboards: latency distributions, token cost, success metrics (exact match / business-defined metrics).
- Tracing hooks: request-level tracing from prompt -> tokens -> model variant, surfaced in the console and exportable to Datadog.
- Rollout guardrails: automatic rollback or canary policies when regression thresholds are exceeded.
- Performance goal: median inference latency < 300ms for the primary triage route in our dedicated environment.

Requested artifacts / asks from ZenHealth (you mentioned today)
- Full golden prompt export (format: CSV with prompt family, expected outputs, fuzz/threshold)
- Security questionnaire (you offered to send SOC2 evidence items)

Next steps (agreed)
1) Aditya to run a 60–90 minute technical deep-dive next week to map tracing hooks and demo dashboard prototypes (proposed slots below).
2) ZenHealth to share the golden prompts CSV and the security questionnaire PDF.
3) Redwood to provision a short trial in Dedicated/Private to run evals against current model snapshot and surface regression stats.
4) Schedule a 30-minute follow-up in ~2 weeks to review demo results and trial metrics.

Proposed windows for the technical deep-dive (PDT):
- Tue 2026-06-30 10:00–11:30
- Wed 2026-07-01 09:00–10:30

Attachments: ZenHealth_Security_Questionnaire_Q1_2026.pdf (attached)

Thanks — excited to partner on making these regression checks and observability first-class.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

---
Note: For the technical deep-dive, Aditya will want examples of the most critical prompt families (as marked in the CSV).

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap, this aligns with our notes. Two quick clarifications:
1) The regression window we care about is: weekly runs that compare model SHA X -> candidate Y on the golden prompts; we need daily alerts for severe regressions (>=5% drop).
2) Our golden prompts export will include tags for "triage", "eligibility", "billing" prompt families.

Attached: ZenHealth_Golden_Prompts_v1.csv
Also attaching the security questionnaire we mentioned (we prefer to receive your SOC2 link or specifics on how Redwood stores logs).

We can do Tue 6/30 at 10:00 PDT — that works for both Priya and me. Please send calendar invite.

Thanks,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Internal: ZenHealth — prep for 6/30 tech deep-dive

Aditya / Lauren — quick internal summary and asks following the discovery call with ZenHealth:

Summary: ZenHealth needs per-prompt observability, automated regression detection against golden prompt sets, tracing hooks to map prompts -> tokens -> model variant, dashboards for cost/latency, and rollout guardrails for canary/auto-rollback. Primary OKR: reduce manual rollbacks and detect regressions within 24 hours.

Aditya: can you prepare the following for the 6/30 deep-dive?
- Demo: tracing hook implementation (show how a single request will surface in the console + export to Datadog).
- Prototype dashboard: latency distribution, token cost per route, regression trend line for golden prompts.
- Short runbook for canary thresholds + automatic rollback example.

Lauren: please pull the SOC2 link and standard security evidence we typically send for Private/Dedicated trials. I attached the questionnaire ZenHealth sent.

Also, we need a short test plan to run their CSV through Redwood Optimize evals — baseline metrics to show in the 2-week follow-up.

Thanks — I will send the calendar invite for 6/30 10:00 PDT once Aditya confirms.

Best,
Marissa

---
Note: keep the demo focused on the triage prompt family first (highest business impact).

I'll also include an example of the regression alert policy we recommend (5% drop threshold + auto-canary pause).
